I don't think it's fair to review bomb Fantasy Life i just because LEVEL-5 is starting to use AI, especially since there is no evidence this specific game was developed using AI.

Fantasy Life i is a wonderful game with a lot of charm. The gameplay can be repetitive, but the variety keeps it fun. Just like in the original, you can be a knight one minute and a cook the next. There is a ton of fun to be had here. This entry in the fantasy Life serie also features a better story, and the "Legend" bosses can be genuinely challenging. I clocked 200 hours in the original and already have 113 hours in this one.

Regarding the AI slop issue:
I will be the first to denounce AI slop, and IF any future DLC turns into AI slop, I will 100% change my review. However, there is a responsible way to use AI. If it's used strictly for polish, it should be fine. In a 3D game, even individual blades of grass

I am a massive fan of the original and I love this game but it feels abandoned to me. This is one of the games that could greatly benefit from more story DLC and content however all we got so far is the base game and a mediocre end game DLC (It was free so I am a lot more lenient on it). We need something like Origin island in the original to expand more on the game.  If you are thinking of buying it then just know that it is a good game but it will get a bit repetitive and you will be wanting more.

I *LOVE* this game, but as someone who put over 2000 hours in the 3DS game (with DLC) I can't help but mention this game has lost some of the charm of the original.. 
But I really want this review to just focus on this game, if you see it on sale and enjoy games that offers simple combat, world exploration, farming crafting materials, crafting, dungeon crawling and even town/house decoration, this game is definitely worth it to pick up! I always have and will continue to refer to Fantasy Life games as 'baby's first MMOPRG' (without the MASSIVE multiplayer) as I really feel like it sums up the big variety of fun mechanics the games offer.

While this game doesn't use AI as according to the steam page, keep in mind the company are using gen AI in some of their game development now, so whether or not you want to support that with your money plays in a factor too for a lot of consumers.

I have a few hundred hours on the 3ds. If you're wanting a experience like that. It's here, but its not one to one. But that doesn't mean that this game is bad.

Personally, I've enjoyed it a lot, but there are things that are left to be desired. 
While it still has the gameplay loop of progressing in one life to help in another life. It just doesn't feel as rewarding. It is very easy to progress the life's, with the only struggle being where to find bosses for the weapon life quests usually. And the new farming and art life's while cool in concept, execution feels bland.
The farming life feels like it should of been more as a side mechanic and not it's own life with levels, quests, and tools. And the art life I feel like could of been genuinely one of the best life's. But instead, it was just a mashup of carpentry and tailoring in my opinion. And I only found it useful for money grindin
Is a steep price, but in my opinion worth the money. Especially if you liked the 3DS game

Grindy. Repetitive. But it's really good! I loved the 3DS version, and when this one reached 30% off I gave in. I'm really enjoying it. There is just so much to do, and there is freedom in choosing what you want to focus on.

Looks and runs great, I had to adjust the HDR settings because the default is a bit overly bright and washed out.

I don't think the deluxe edition is worth that much extra money, but I bought it anyway because I didn't want to feel I was missing out.

It still scratches that old 3DS itch, but the new systems drag it straight into bad mobile game territory. I kept waiting for a pop-up to flash mid-session and offer a starter pack. As a fan of Fantasy Life on 3ds, this game is worse in almost every aspect when it comes to difficulty and variety. Bosses tend to be reskins with the same 3 abilities. I should not be able to defeat a level 50 boss at level 15. I remember getting my ass kicked on 3ds for not being geared up enough or being roughly the same level as a boss. Monsters to kill for each combat Life are also about 80% the same. What happened to variety?

After ~38 hours (and grinding every job to Expert, mind you, I'm probably halfway through), story is still bland and rather boring. And I love dragons, I'm all here for dragons. The dragon is the most interesting part of the game.

reviews.title: Animal Crossing if it was fun
reviews.text: I was skeptical at first because the App Store page didn't reflect the game very well. I'm glad I gave it a shot because it has genuinely rewarding and satisfying RNG + PvE elements plus much more content than I had initially anticipated. It has many mechanics similar to Animal Crossing but goes way farther in depth in a much more interactive experience. There's crafting, a bunch of different skills (lives) to level up with their own unlocks, you get your own island to build and decorate, and there's tons of different monsters (including bosses) that all have different drop tables that include rare items and gear. I am not exaggerating when I say this game is absolutely filled with content. The price is definitely worth it for this PC/ console game that runs surprisingly well on an IPhone.

reviews.title: Amazing port of Fantasy Life i: The Girl Who Steals Time
reviews.text:
This is a straight port of game that released last year on pc and consoles, at a fraction of the price! Anyone interested in this game just needs to search and read/watch reviews - there are plenty. In short- the game is part Rune Factory, Animal Crossing, and RuneScape with a sprinkle of Zelda. 

The touchscreen controls work very well in my opinion and it’s a perfect game to play for both short and long bursts. It’s a great fit for phones and having the ability to play this game truly anywhere on the fly is great!

It also has cross saves and cross play with the pc and console versions. The price of $25 may be steep for the mobile market, but you’re getting a full game that has all the same content as its $60 base game counterpart on pc and consoles. This is a steal!
